social.title: Midnight Run to the Frontier
social.description: The correct end to any night in Albuquerque: fluorescent light, a tortilla machine going, and the entire city's post-last-call population in one room.
social.bonus: Order at the counter without looking at the menu board.

social.title: Balloon Glow After Dark
social.description: Hundreds of tethered balloons firing their burners in unison after sunset, turning a dark field into a city of glowing lanterns you can walk between.
social.bonus: Stand close enough to feel the heat off a burner.

social.title: Sold-Out Night at the Sunshine Theater
social.description: A 1924 downtown theatre turned mid-size rock room, where the balcony is the move and the floor is a mess in the best way.
social.bonus: Watch one song from the balcony, the rest from the floor.

social.title: Taproom Night at Marble Downtown
social.description: The flagship of the brewery that anchors New Mexico beer, with a rooftop deck over downtown and live music most nights.
social.bonus: Get on the roof before the sun drops behind the West Mesa.

social.title: Rack 'Em at Anodyne
social.description: An upstairs dive on Central with a long row of pool tables, a deep whiskey shelf and zero interest in impressing anyone.
social.bonus: Play a stranger for the table and mean it.

social.title: Show at the El Rey Theater
social.description: A 1941 Central Avenue movie house that now books everything from Earl Sweatshirt to hardcore, with original deco bones still intact.
social.bonus: Look up at the ceiling before the lights go down.

social.title: Isotopes Game at Isotopes Park
social.description: Minor league baseball named after a Simpsons joke, played in front of a berm with the Sandias behind the outfield and green chile on everything.
social.bonus: Sit on the grass berm instead of a seat.

social.title: Rooftop Cocktails at the Apothecary Lounge
social.description: Prohibition-era drinks on the roof of a 1926 hospital-turned-hotel, with the Sandias east and downtown west, and a table made from a 1940s coffin carrier.
social.bonus: Order something made with the Aztec chocolate bitters.

social.title: Tractor Brewing in Wells Park
social.description: A scrappy 4th Street taproom that runs burlesque, bluegrass jams, drag and vinyl nights, and stays open to two at weekends.
social.bonus: Go on a night you'd normally avoid and stay for the whole thing.

social.title: Loud Show at the Launchpad
social.description: A battered Central Avenue room that has taken punk, metal and hip-hop through Albuquerque for decades, with the sound to match.
social.bonus: Stand in the front third and accept what happens.

social.title: Cantina Night at El Pinto
social.description: The cantina side of the North Valley institution — fire pits, string lights through the cottonwoods, and margaritas by the pitcher.
social.bonus: Claim a spot at a fire pit and hold it all night.

social.title: Touring Band at Sister Bar
social.description: Downtown's indie living room — local taps, a back patio, and a stage small enough that the band drinks at the bar afterwards.
social.bonus: Buy the opener's record, not the headliner's.

adventure.title: Hike the Pino Trail into the Sandias
adventure.description: A steady, quiet climb out of Elena Gallegos through piñon and into fir forest, with far fewer people on it than La Luz and almost as much payoff.
adventure.bonus: Keep going past the point where you planned to turn around.

adventure.title: Read the Rock at Boca Negra Canyon
adventure.description: Twenty-four thousand petroglyphs carved into volcanic escarpment by Ancestral Pueblo and early Spanish hands — a short scramble puts you face to face with them.
adventure.bonus: Find a glyph nobody has photographed and don't post it.

adventure.title: Ride the Sandia Peak Tramway to the Crest
adventure.description: Fifteen minutes and 4,000 vertical feet on the longest aerial tramway in the Americas, ending on a 10,378-foot ridge with eleven thousand square miles in view.
adventure.bonus: Ride up in daylight and come down after dark.

adventure.title: Sunrise Balloon Flight with Rainbow Ryders
adventure.description: Albuquerque is the ballooning capital of the world for a reason — the box wind pattern lets a pilot steer you out over the Rio Grande and back again.
adventure.bonus: Ask the pilot to explain the Albuquerque Box mid-flight.

adventure.title: Session the Walls at Stone Age
adventure.description: New Mexico's big climbing gym, with a first-timer lesson thrown in free and rental gear, for the days the desert is too hot to touch rock.
adventure.bonus: Top out a route without looking down once.

adventure.title: Cruise the Paseo del Bosque Trail
adventure.description: Sixteen uninterrupted miles under cottonwoods along the Rio Grande — no road crossings the entire way, which is the whole point.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full length without stopping for a light, because there aren't any.

adventure.title: Walk the Ruins at Salinas Pueblo Missions
adventure.description: Three 17th-century Spanish mission churches standing roofless over abandoned Pueblo villages an hour south — enormous, silent, and almost always empty of people.
adventure.bonus: Stand in the middle of the Quarai nave and say nothing for a full minute.

adventure.title: Sunset on the Albuquerque Volcanoes
adventure.description: Five extinct cinder cones on the West Mesa, facing back across the whole city to the Sandias as they turn watermelon-pink at dusk.
adventure.bonus: Stay up there until the streetlights come on below you.

adventure.title: Breaking Bad RV Tour
adventure.description: Three hours in a replica of that RV, hitting twenty-plus filming locations with lunch at the actual Los Pollos Hermanos — shameless and completely worth it.
adventure.bonus: Order exactly what Gus would serve you.

adventure.title: Walk the Slot Canyon at Tent Rocks
adventure.description: A narrow slot squeezes you between volcanic walls, then opens onto a field of cone-shaped hoodoos left by a seven-million-year-old eruption.
adventure.bonus: Touch both walls at the tightest point in the slot.

adventure.title: Mass Ascension at the Balloon Fiesta
adventure.description: Five hundred balloons inflating around you in the dark, then rising in waves over nine days every October — the largest ballooning event on earth, and you walk the field among them.
adventure.bonus: Be on the field for Dawn Patrol, before the sun is up.

adventure.title: Ski Sandia Peak Above the City
adventure.description: A small, deeply local hill on the back side of the Sandias where you can ski in the morning and be eating green chile in town by two.
adventure.bonus: Take one lap off the summit chair, whatever the conditions.

adventure.title: Climb the La Luz Trail
adventure.description: Eight miles and nearly 4,000 feet from desert scrub to alpine forest on the Sandias' west face — the hardest, most honest way to reach the crest.
adventure.bonus: Hike up and take the tram down. You've earned it.

adventure.title: Drive the Turquoise Trail to Madrid
adventure.description: Fifty miles of high-desert byway past ghost mining towns to Madrid, a coal camp that emptied out and came back as a street of galleries and bikers.
adventure.bonus: Buy something from the first gallery you walk into.

adventure.title: Climb the Crest Road on a Bike
adventure.description: Thirteen and a half miles of switchbacks up NM-536 to the Sandia Crest — one of the great road climbs in the Southwest, topping out above ten thousand feet.
adventure.bonus: Don't put a foot down before the summit car park.

adventure.title: Ride the Foothills at Elena Gallegos
adventure.description: Singletrack straight off the city's eastern edge into the Sandia foothills, with the whole grid spread out below and the mountain wall right above.
adventure.bonus: Ride until you can't see a single building.

culture.title: Galleries and Studios in Old Town
culture.description: The streets off the plaza are thick with working Pueblo and Hispanic artists selling jewellery, pottery and santos directly, with no gallery cut.
culture.bonus: Buy one piece straight from the person who made it.

culture.title: Native Dances at the Indian Pueblo Cultural Center
culture.description: Owned and run by New Mexico's nineteen Pueblos — their own account of their own history, with live dance performances in the courtyard most weekends.
culture.bonus: Stay for a full dance set and put your phone away for it.

culture.title: Hot Air History at the Balloon Museum
culture.description: A purpose-built museum beside Balloon Fiesta Park covering everything from the Montgolfiers to the gondolas flown across the Pacific — several of them hanging overhead.
culture.bonus: Find the balloon that actually crossed an ocean.

culture.title: Four Centuries at the Albuquerque Museum
culture.description: The city's own museum in Old Town, strong on Spanish colonial armour, Taos painters and how this valley actually came to be settled.
culture.bonus: Pick the one object you'd steal and justify it out loud.

culture.title: The Torreón Fresco at the National Hispanic Cultural Center
culture.description: A concrete tower in Barelas holding one of the largest concave frescoes in North America — four thousand square feet of Hispanic history, painted over ten years.
culture.bonus: Lie on the floor and look straight up.

culture.title: Pueblo Deco at the KiMo Theatre
culture.description: A 1927 picture palace built in the only architectural style native to New Mexico — buffalo skulls, Navajo motifs and air vents shaped like Zia symbols.
culture.bonus: Find the plaster longhorn skulls with glowing amber eyes.

culture.title: Seismosaurus at the Natural History Museum
culture.description: New Mexico dug up some of the strangest dinosaurs on record, and this museum walks you through five billion years of the state's geology to get to them.
culture.bonus: Stand under the biggest skeleton and look straight up.

culture.title: Deep Time at the Maxwell Museum
culture.description: A free anthropology museum on the UNM campus with an archaeology collection covering eleven thousand years of people in the Southwest.
culture.bonus: Find the oldest human-made object on display.

chill.title: Pedal Boats at Tingley Beach
chill.description: Three fishing ponds and a pedal-boat lake in the bosque, with the Sandias on the horizon and absolutely nothing demanded of you.
chill.bonus: Race another boat across the lake and lose gracefully.

chill.title: Nob Hill Neon at Dusk
chill.description: A dense stretch of original Route 66 where the restored motel and shop neon comes on all at once — best walked slowly, with no destination.
chill.bonus: Photograph the ugliest sign you can find.

chill.title: Sketch in the Albuquerque Museum Sculpture Garden
chill.description: Four acres of outdoor sculpture beside the museum in Old Town, free to walk, with cottonwood shade and almost nobody in it on a weekday.
chill.bonus: Draw one sculpture badly and keep the drawing.

chill.title: Old Town Plaza and San Felipe de Neri
chill.description: The 1706 founding square of the city, built around a church that has held services continuously for three hundred years, ringed by adobe and portal shade.
chill.bonus: Step inside the church and sit in a back pew for five minutes.

chill.title: Boardwalk at the Rio Grande Nature Center
chill.description: A half-buried visitor centre with a glass wall onto a duck pond, and a boardwalk out into the cottonwood bosque where sandhill cranes overwinter.
chill.bonus: Sit at the glass wall until you've identified three different birds.

chill.title: Walk the Lavender Rows at Los Poblanos
chill.description: Twenty-five acres of lavender and formal gardens laid out by John Gaw Meem, fifteen minutes from downtown and completely silent.
chill.bonus: Buy one thing from the farm shop made with what's growing outside.

chill.title: Lose the Afternoon in the Botanic Garden
chill.description: A walled Spanish-Moorish garden, a glass conservatory of desert plants and a Japanese garden, all tucked against the Rio Grande.
chill.bonus: Find the quietest bench in the whole garden and stay there.

chill.title: Picnic in the Cottonwood Bosque
chill.description: The Rio Grande's cottonwood forest runs the whole length of the city — step off the trail, find a clearing, and the town disappears entirely.
chill.bonus: Go far enough in that you can't hear a single car.

chill.title: Day Drinking at Canteen Brewhouse
chill.description: Albuquerque's oldest brewery, still in an unglamorous industrial building off Aztec Road, with a patio built for killing an entire afternoon.
chill.bonus: Drink whatever the bartender is personally into right now.

chill.title: Sunset from the Sandia Crest Deck
chill.description: Over ten thousand feet up with a railing, a horizon a hundred miles wide, and the whole Rio Grande valley turning gold beneath you.
chill.bonus: Stay past sunset and watch the city lights come up all at once.

foodie.title: Brunch at The Grove Cafe & Market
foodie.description: The bright, loud daytime anchor of the EDo district — farm eggs, good pastry and a market counter, all closed by two in the afternoon.
foodie.bonus: Add the farm-fresh egg to whatever you ordered.

foodie.title: Dinner on the Farm at Farm & Table
foodie.description: A North Valley restaurant sitting on its own working acreage, where the menu turns over with whatever came out of the field that week.
foodie.bonus: Ask which dish came off their own land today and order that.

foodie.title: Carne Adovada at Mary & Tito's
foodie.description: A James Beard America's Classic since 1963, where the red chile is the whole argument and the turnovers are the correct order.
foodie.bonus: Order it both ways — plate and turnover — and settle it for yourself.

foodie.title: Dinner at Ten Thousand Feet at TEN 3
foodie.description: A restaurant you can only reach by cable car, hanging off the Sandia Crest with the entire Rio Grande valley going dark through the glass.
foodie.bonus: Time your reservation so dessert lands at sunset.

foodie.title: Five A.M. Breakfast Burrito at the Frontier
foodie.description: Open since 1971 across from UNM, with hand-rolled tortillas, a John Wayne shrine and a sweet roll that has ruined people's diets for fifty years.
foodie.bonus: Get the sweet roll, extra butter, no negotiation.

foodie.title: Lunch Counter at Duran Central Pharmacy
foodie.description: Walk past the prescription counter of a 1942 pharmacy and sit at New Mexico's oldest lunch counter for hand-rolled tortillas and serious chile.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter, not a table, and order the carne adovada.

foodie.title: Field-to-Fork Dinner at Campo
foodie.description: Dinner in a 1930s dairy barn on a working 25-acre lavender farm, with most of the plate grown within sight of the table.
foodie.bonus: Walk the lavender rows before you sit down.

foodie.title: Stuffed Sopaipilla at Sadie's
foodie.description: A New Mexican institution that started in a bowling alley — the salsa arrives hot enough to be a warning and the stuffed sopaipilla is the size of a shoebox.
foodie.bonus: Finish the whole sopaipilla. Nobody does.

foodie.title: Biscochitos at Golden Crown Panaderia
foodie.description: A family bakery since 1972 turning out the official state cookie, green chile bread and pizza from a beehive oven in the back garden.
foodie.bonus: Order the green chile bread and eat a slice standing in the car park.

foodie.title: Give the Password at Vernon's Speakeasy
foodie.description: An unmarked door in the North Valley that genuinely asks you for a password, then opens onto a dim steakhouse with live music and no sense of irony.
foodie.bonus: Get the password in advance and deliver it with a straight face.

foodie.title: Patio Margaritas at El Pinto
foodie.description: Twelve acres of cottonwood-shaded courtyards in the North Valley, a salsa line sold nationwide, and the single best patio in New Mexico.
foodie.bonus: Get the chile both red and green and finish the sopaipilla.

foodie.title: Sunday at the Rail Yards Market
foodie.description: Two hundred growers, makers and cooks filling a cathedral-sized 1920s locomotive repair shop in Barelas every Sunday morning.
foodie.bonus: Eat something you can't name from a stall with no English sign.

8ball.title: Red or Green
8ball.description: Wildcard: New Mexico's official state question. Eat at three different places in one day and order red at one, green at the next, Christmas at the last — then pick a side for life.
8ball.bonus: Commit to your answer out loud and never change it.

8ball.title: Chase the Watermelon Light
8ball.description: Wildcard: the Sandias turn deep pink for about ten minutes at sunset — sandia means watermelon. Find somewhere in the city you've never stood and be there for it.
8ball.bonus: Get it on camera without a single building in frame.
